### Summary

When a HTTP proxy environment variable, e. g. `HTTP_PROXY` is set, then `uv` will use that proxy. However that happens silently, even in the verbose output.

Due to the pecularities of `uv`'s Rust network stack it won't be able to resolve single label names. So if `HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy` is set this leads to the following error:
```
$ uv lock --upgrade-package lxml
  cause: Failed to fetch:
         https://devpi.local/lst/stable/+simple/requests-oauthlib/
  cause: error sending request for url
         (https://devpi.local/lst/stable/+simple/requests-oauthlib/)
  cause: client error (Connect)
  cause: tunnel error: failed to create underlying connection
  cause: dns error
  cause: error resolving DNS
  cause: failed to lookup address information: Name does not resolve
```
The resources given in the error message work entirely fine. So the DNS error looks pretty weird. After serious headscratching it turns out that it's actually true that there was a DNS error and the issue is that the name of the proxy can't be resolved since it has only one label. When setting `HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.local` it will work fine.

This only happens with `musl` builds of `uv`, as installed through the distroless docker image. On `Glibc` based systems it doesn't happen when `uv` is installed through `pip`, as this results in a version without the problematic code. It uses `Glibc` instead, which is able to resolve single label names.

Please make a clearer error message in this case. If the problem is actually the connection to the proxy then explicitly state that and mention the proxy's URL instead, or in addition to, the URL that was attempted to load through it.

### Platform

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), Linux 5.14.0-741.22.1.el9_9.x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.13.9 (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl)

### Python version

Python 3.14.9
